inputs.text: They’re presenting it as an anti-corruption effort, but the real issue is who gets to set the rules. On 25 March 2026 in Paris, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader watching. It’s not just about transparency: it gives an outside institution influence over how the country is governed, while the language of “integrity” makes that influence sound unquestionable.
